subject: Follow-up: log integrity confirmation and data impact for Nov 20 incident
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@fintechcorp.com>, FinTechCorp Security <sec@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:23:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: log integrity confirmation and data impact for Nov 20 incident

Lena / FinTech security team —

Thanks again for your patience while we investigated the service disruption on Nov 20. Our initial takeaway from the first-pass triage: the incident was caused by a degraded caching layer that led to elevated error rates for a subset of customers between 14:42–15:06 UTC. We escalated to infra and security immediately.

Action so far (short):
- Full collection of service and host logs for the window (14:30–15:30 UTC)
- S3 access and object metadata snapshots preserved (object versions retained)
- KMS and audit trail pulled for relevant keys and user principals

To be explicit about the question I expect you to ask: we have no evidence to date of data exfiltration or customer data deletion. That said, we want to confirm integrity with you — we will produce a short statement showing: hashes of objects at rest, S3 access events, and audit logs for read/write for the window.

Stephanie is leading the technical verification; Marcus assisted with log preservation. I expect a preliminary log summary within 2–3 hours and a formal integrity statement by Monday 11/22.

Please let me know if you need anything different (e.g., a transfer of artifacts to a secure bucket you own, or a notarized checksum file).

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales (EMEA & Strategic Accounts)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: (pending) redwood_incident_20261120_log_summary.pdf (will be attached in follow-up)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@fintechcorp.com>, FinTechCorp Security <sec@fintechcorp.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: log integrity confirmation and data impact for Nov 20 incident

Vivek / team —

Quick technical note from the forensics run I finished:
- Timeline: 14:41:32 UTC first error spike; peak errors 14:47:10–14:52:00 UTC; normalization at ~15:05 UTC once the cache nodes were rolled.
- Log sources collected: application logs (stdout/stderr), request traces with request IDs, S3 access logs (server access), KMS audit entries, IAM/STS token issuance logs, and host syslogs.
- Access characteristics: all S3 GET/HEAD operations in the window were attributed to service principals (redwood-service-account-*) and no external IPs were observed in object GET calls for customer buckets. We also checked presigned URL issuance records — none were created during the window.
- Integrity checks: we computed SHA256 hashes of object versions for the affected buckets and compared to the pre-incident snapshot (backups). All hashes match for the sampled set (full CSV attached).

I'm attaching the initial log summary and the s3_access_hashes CSV. No evidence of object deletion or anomalous external downloads. We will continue to expand the sample set and can export signed checksums to a customer-owned bucket if desired.

Attachment: redwood_incident_20261120_log_summary.pdf; s3_access_hashes_20261120.csv

—Stephanie
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Lena Park <lena.park@fintechcorp.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinTechCorp Security <sec@fintechcorp.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:40:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: log integrity confirmation and data impact for Nov 20 incident

Vivek / Stephanie —

Thanks for the quick work. A couple of clarifying requests from our side to satisfy our internal auditors:
1) Can you provide the exact object keys and timestamps you sampled for the SHA256 comparison (not just counts)? We need to map them back to our retention records.
2) Can you confirm whether any requests in the window originated from IP ranges outside of Redwood or from new, previously unseen service principals?
3) For the integrity statement, are you able to include a signed PDF with the hashes and an explanation of methods used (hash algorithm, time of snapshot, who signed)?

If you can share the artifacts to our secure bucket (s3://fintechcorp-evidence/2026-11-20) we will pick them up and ingest into our EDR.

Lena
Director, InfoSec
FinTechCorp

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 16:02, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (attached log summary)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@fintechcorp.com>, FinTechCorp Security <sec@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:15:30 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: log integrity confirmation and data impact for Nov 20 incident

Lena —

Answers inline:
1) Exact sample: attached CSV contains object_key, version_id, snapshot_timestamp_utc, sha256_hash. Sample rows include:
   - customers/fintechcorp/prod/model_inputs/2026-11-20-14-35-02.json, v3, 2026-11-20T14:35:02Z, <hash>
   - customers/fintechcorp/prod/model_outputs/2026-11-20-14-47-45.bin, v1, 2026-11-20T14:47:45Z, <hash>
(Full list in s3_access_hashes_20261120.csv attached).

2) IP/service principal: we observed only internal Redwood service principal calls (redwood-service-account-1..6). No external IP ranges made GET/HEAD calls against FinTechCorp buckets in the window. Network flow logs (VPC flow) show normal egress to known CDNs; there are no unexpected egress destinations.

3) Signed PDF: yes — we will produce an integrity_statement_fintechcorp_20261122.pdf that includes methods (SHA256 over object bytes, snapshot times, signer identity), signed by our security lead and timestamped. We can push the artifacts to s3://fintechcorp-evidence/2026-11-20 as a secure, customer-owned ingestion if you provide a write temp token or we can transfer via secure share.

Next steps:
- I will finalize the signed PDF and push to your bucket Saturday night (UTC) if you confirm access.
- We'll retain all collected logs for 90 days and put the forensics ticket on high-visibility until 2027-02-20.

—Stephanie

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@fintechcorp.com>, FinTechCorp Security <sec@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 11:30:00 +0000
Subject: Final integrity confirmation and artifacts delivery

Lena / FinTech security team —

Attached is the formal integrity statement for the Nov 20 event (integrity_statement_fintechcorp_20261122.pdf). Summary points:
- We confirm that, after a full forensic review of application logs, S3 server access logs, KMS audit logs, IAM issuance records, and network flows for the incident window, there is no evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized access, or object deletion affecting FinTechCorp customer data.
- SHA256 checksums were calculated against preserved object versions and compared to pre-incident backups — no mismatches were found in the sampled and full verification sets. CSV of object keys + hashes attached.
- All artifacts (signed PDF, CSV, raw log bundles) have been staged at your requested location: s3://fintechcorp-evidence/2026-11-20. We used server-side encryption (AES256) for the transfer and provided a time-limited write token; please confirm receipt once ingested.

If your auditors need chain-of-custody details, we can provide additional metadata (who accessed which files and timestamps) under a bilateral data handling agreement — happy to coordinate.

Thank you for working with us on this. We will follow-up with the postmortem report and remediation changes (cache health checks, improved circuit breakers) and will share an executive summary by EOD 11/24.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales (EMEA & Strategic Accounts)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: integrity_statement_fintechcorp_20261122.pdf; s3_access_hashes_20261120.csv
